result.title: Two Actions from One State: Fork Futures Teach JEPA World Models to Compare
result.summary: JEPA world models are trained to predict logged transitions but used to compare counterfactual actions from one state. The logged behavior data show one action per state, and under a local linear approximation we prove the action response is unidentified along any direction the policy never varies within a state. We therefore supplement behavior data with measured outcomes of alternative actions from the same state. Our fork futures execute two actions from one restored state, and their outcome difference cancels the state term, identifying the action response on the sampled span. The resulting model, Fork-JEPA, matches predicted to measured differences, anchors the logged successor with behavior prediction, and adds a lookback head that keeps the predecessor recoverable, all at training time, leaving planning unchanged. On three visual control tasks, behavior-only training leaves the predicted action effect no better than a constant guess. Fork-JEPA makes it readable and raises planning success by up to 14\% over LeWM, its base model. Where the action response changes across hidden zones, it nearly doubles cross-zone success, and 1,024 fork pairs beat 1.2M extra behavior steps. Our project is available at https://fork-jepa.github.io/.

AI.brief_summary: 论文指出现有 JEPA 世界模型只用单动作行为数据训练，局部线性近似下动作响应沿策略不变方向不可辨识；为此从同一恢复状态执行两个动作（fork futures），用结果差抵消状态项，并在训练期加入行为预测锚定与保持前驱可恢复的 lookback head，在三个视觉控制任务上提升规划成功率。
AI.relevance_reason: 成对反事实轨迹相减以消除状态项、并借可回溯头抑制 latent 信息坍缩，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态的贡献分配与视觉信息保留监督提供可核查线索，但该工作属视觉控制世界模型，与 VLM 生成式推理仍有距离。
